items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: when we won the championship, Mel Allen came and gave us — we got trophies for different things that we had done.

ctx.x: I played shortstop or third base. I was never a long ball hitter but I could place hit pretty well. And when we won the championship, Mel Allen came and gave us — we got trophies for different things that we had done. It was very nice.
How has the work scene changed for you, like in the last ten years? Do you pick and choose a little more than usual?

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I got a batting trophy from Mel Allen.

ctx.x: I was going to ask you, did you play in any of the jazz leagues or the Broadway show leagues?

Yeah. I was in that when it started, when it was formed by John Effrat, who conceived the idea of having each theater have a ball team and playing in Central Park for fun. I was out there. I was with the Cole Porter show, Silk Stockings, and we won the championship that year. I got a batting trophy from Mel Allen. Some of the other guys on

the team did. We had some girls on the team too. Joe Harris was on the team. Artie Rubin, who could hit a ball out of the park on demand, almost. We had – Art Lund was playing with us. It was fantastic. We had some wonderful people out there.
